cards.body: - 기사 스크랩 - 댓글 - 공유 - 글자크기 - 프린트 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. 엔비디아, 네이버 3대주주로 3자 연합모델로 안정성·경쟁력 확보 네이버는 “브룩필드로부터 90억달러 규모의 컴퓨팅 인프라를 확보하는 계약을 맺었다”며 “엔비디아의 전략적 지분 투자를 위한 선결 조건을 충족했다”고 27일 공시했다. 계약에 따라 브룩필드는 특수목적법인(SPV)인 ‘에셋코(Asset Co.)’를 설립하고 그래픽처리장치(GPU)와 데이터센터 등 컴퓨팅 인프라 자산을 네이버에 제공한다. 구체적인 GPU와 데이터센터의 규모 및 비중은 공개하지 않았다. 네이버는 이렇게 확보한 GPU와 데이터센터 등으로 가칭 ‘네이버 AI팩토리’를 운영하면서 국내 대기업 고객사에 AI 컴퓨팅 서비스를 판매하는 역할을 맡는다. 매출이 발생할 때마다 에셋코에 사용료를 지급하는 구조다. 네이버 AI팩토리 운영은 네이버클라우드가 주도하기로 했다. 네이버는 대기업 고객사 여러 곳과 계약 협상을 진행 중인 것으로 전해졌다. 이번 계약으로 네이버는 엔비디아를 대상으로 한 10억달러 규모 제3자 배정 유상증자 절차에도 속도를 낼 방침이다. 증자가 완료되면 엔비디아는 네이버 주식 4.5%(신주 724만1564주)를 취득해 국민연금, 블랙록에 이은 3대주주에 오른다. 네이버와 엔비디아, 브룩필드 3자 연합의 ‘AI 팩토리’ 사업의 핵심은 자본·기술·운영 역량을 나눠 맡는 구조에 있다. 엔비디아는 자본과 차세대 고성능 컴퓨팅 플랫폼 관련 기술 협력을 제공하고, 브룩필드는 GPU와 데이터센터 등 인프라 자산을 확보해 제공하는 역할을 맡는다. 네이버는 대규모 데이터센터를 직접 건립하거나 GPU를 매입하는 데 필요한 초기 자금 부담을 줄이면서 AI 인프라 사업을 신성장 동력으로 확보할 수 있게 됐다. 엔비디아는 자사 기술 기반의 컴퓨팅 인프라 생태계를 확장하고, 브룩필드는 인프라 투자 자산에서 수익을 창출하는 구조다. 글로벌 클라우드·AI 인프라 기업들이 대규모 투자에 따른 자금 조달 부담을 안고 있는 상황에서 이번 사업 모델에도 관심이 쏠린다. 글로벌 네오클라우드 기업 코어위브는 한때 회사채 금리가 15%까지 치솟으며 자금 조달 비용에 대한 우려가 부각됐다. 업계에서는 AI 인프라 경쟁의 무게중심이 단순한 설비 확충에서 투자 효율과 재무 안정성으로 옮겨갈 수 있다는 전망이 나온다. 업계 관계자는 “3자 연합 구조가 가진 재무적 안정성은 글로벌 투자 시장에서 새로운 대안으로 떠오를 수 있다”고 말했다. 투자은행(IB) 업계 관계자도 “지금까지는 누가 더 많은 빚을 내 칩을 확보하느냐는 규모의 경쟁이었다면, 이제는 재무 리스크를 관리하면서 얼마나 효율적으로 인프라를 운용하느냐의 구조적 경쟁으로 진화하고 있다”고 했다. 정지은 기자 jeong@hankyung.com 한경 프리미엄9의 모든 콘텐츠는 한국경제신문의 저작물로 저작권법의 보호를 받습니다. 사전 허가 없는 무단 전재·복제·배포·캡처 공유·AI 학습 활용 및 상업적 이용을 금합니다. 위반 시 서비스 이용 제한 및 민형사상 법적 책임이 발생할 수 있습니다.

key_facts: NVIDIA가 **Meta의 975억 달러 규모 지분 공모에 30억 달러를 투자**한다.
Meta는 Vera Rubin, Vera CPU, Spectrum-X 이더넷, BlueField-4 DPU 등 NVIDIA 하드웨어 배치를 확대할 계획이다.
양사는 NVIDIA의 **OpenShell 및 Sentry**를 활용해 AI 에이전트의 안전한 배치를 위한 추가 협력을 검토 중이다.
Meta는 공모 규모를 975억 달러로 확대했으며, 이 중 250억 달러는 보통주, 125억 달러는 전환우선주(건당 50달러, 2.5억 주)로 조달된다.
Meta의 Muse는 2026년 9월 출시된 개인용 AI 에이전트로, 전용 가상머신(VM)에서 사용자 데이터와 함께 구동된다.
summary_data.why_matters: 이번 투자는 NVIDIA가 단순 하드웨어 공급자에서 AI 에이전트 생태계의 전략적 파트너로 지위를 강화하는 사례다. **에이전트형 컴퓨팅이라는 새로운 패러다임**에서 NVIDIA의 풀스택 인프라(GPU·DPU·네트워킹)가 하이퍼스케일러의 핵심 기반으로 자리잡고 있음을 보여준다.
summary_data.subject_angle: NVIDIA는 하드웨어 판매를 넘어 **지분 투자를 통한 고객사와의 수요 선순환 구조**를 구축하며, OpenShell·Sentry 같은 안전성 소프트웨어 스택으로 에이전트 AI 시장의 표준을 선점하려는 전략을 보인다.
summary_data.focus_angle: Vera Rubin, Spectrum-X, BlueField-4로 구성된 end-to-end 에이전트 인프라는 **자율주행 및 로보틱스에서 요구되는 실시간 추론·안전 검증 아키텍처**와 기술적으로 맞닿아 있어, NVIDIA가 완성차 OEM·휴머노이드 기업에 동일한 에이전트 컴퓨팅 스택을 확장 적용할 가능성을 시사한다. 특히 Sentry와 같은 안전 배치 기술은 자율주행·휴머노이드 로봇의 기능안전(functional safety) 요구와 연결될 수 있다.

cards.body: Nvidia will invest $3 billion in Meta’s equity offering as part of an expanded partnership between the two companies, focused on Meta’s Muse family of AI agents. The partners will collaborate on “optimizations across workflows” to boost inference and training performance and improve total cost of ownership, Nvidia said. Under the terms of the agreement, Meta will expand its deployment of Nvidia hardware, including Vera Rubin and Vera CPUs, Spectrum-X Ethernet networking technology, and BlueField-4 DPUs. The companies also said they would consider “additional collaboration opportunities” centered around Nvidia’s OpenShell and Sentry offerings to support the safe deployment of AI agents. “AI agents represent a new computing paradigm — software that understands our goals, reasons, uses tools and gets work done on our behalf,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of Nvidia. “This changes how we use computers, from operating applications to working with intelligent agents. Nvidia and Meta are expanding our partnership to optimize the computing infrastructure end-to-end for capable, efficient and secure AI agents, so Muse can empower billions of people to achieve more and pursue greater ambitions.” The news follows an announcement from Meta on October 26 that the company had raised the size of its planned equity offering to $97.5bn. Of that total, $25bn will be raised through common stock, with an additional $12.5bn to be raised through the sale of 250 million convertible preferred depositary shares at $50 each. Meta is also planning to sell up to $60bn in shares after its planned non-voting Class C shares start trading in the first quarter of 2027. Meta introduced its Muse AI agent in September 2026. Described by the company as a personal AI agent “that proactively helps with people’s goals and suggests ideas.” It runs on a dedicated virtual machine (VM) that plays host to both the agent and a user’s data. While the agent was first introduced to the consumer market primarily through the Tamagotchi-like Charm device, Meta has also debuted a version of Muse designed for small and medium enterprises that incorporates tools such as Dropbox, Slack, and Zoom into Muse’s agentic workflow. cards.body: NVIDIA and Oracle today announced plans to expand Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Superclusters with NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems to multi-gigawatt scale, supporting growing customer demand for AI training, inference and agentic applications. Oracle and NVIDIA also expanded their AI infrastructure collaboration with the general availability of NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 and NVIDIA Vera CPUs on OCI. The expanded collaboration gives customers infrastructure for both the GPU-intensive work of training and serving frontier models and the CPU-intensive tasks agents perform between model calls, including executing tools, testing code and retrieving data. Customers can scale CPU and GPU resources independently to match their workloads, helping reduce idle capacity and put more of their infrastructure to productive use. OCI Superclusters Help Organizations Bring Frontier AI to Market Faster at Multi-Gigawatt Scale OCI Superclusters combine NVIDIA NVL72 rack-scale systems, Oracle Acceleron networking with NVIDIA Spectrum-X™ Ethernet networking featuring NVIDIA Spectrum™-6 switches and NVIDIA BlueField®-4 DPUs, and gigawatt-class power and cooling to train and serve the largest AI models. Each rack connects 72 GPUs through NVIDIA NVLink™ scale-up networking, while OCI’s resilient, multiplanar network scales across hundreds of thousands of GPUs. The planned Vera Rubin expansion builds on OCI’s existing NVIDIA-powered infrastructure, including NVIDIA GB200 and GB300 NVL72 systems. NVIDIA’s common CUDA® software foundation and continued software optimization help customers support evolving models and workloads across hardware generations. OCI also plans to introduce NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8, delivering eight Rubin GPUs connected through NVLink in an x86-based server configuration. The planned platform features two 64-core Intel Xeon 6 CPUs, 4TB of DDR5 memory and 6.4 Tbps of high-speed RDMA networking, providing a flexible deployment option for AI training, fine-tuning and inference. HGX Rubin NVL8 enables customers to adopt next-generation Rubin GPU technology in a smaller eight-GPU configuration while maintaining compatibility with x86-based applications. This flexibility enables customers to adapt their AI infrastructure to different models and workloads as their needs evolve, using accelerated computing capacity across both training and inference to make better use of their infrastructure investments. OpenAI has demonstrated how this infrastructure supports frontier AI. cards.body: News Summary: - NVIDIA and Meta will expand their partnership on Muse and the Muse family of models, reflecting popular demand for AI agents. - The companies are also considering other technological collaborations, including NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture to strengthen agency security and NVIDIA Sentry for monitoring, structured, unstructured and graph data processing. - Meta to expand NVIDIA Vera Rubin and Vera CPU deployment to boost performance and scale workloads with NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet networking and BlueField-4. NVIDIA and Meta today announced they will partner to expand their work on Muse and the Muse family of models to improve inference and training performance, reflecting popular demand for useful AI agents. Meta’s Muse models and agents, which leverage NVIDIA’s infrastructure, have delivered frontier-level benchmark performance and surging consumer downloads since launch. Meta and NVIDIA intend to further deepen their collaboration by partnering on optimizations across workflows to maximize performance and improve total cost of ownership. Meta and NVIDIA will also consider additional collaboration opportunities with NVIDIA on its NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture, including NVIDIA OpenShell™ for safe deployment and NVIDIA Sentry for monitoring agent behavior. This announcement reinforces Meta and NVIDIA’s strong long-term partnership to support Meta’s AI infrastructure ambitions. Meta intends to expand the deployment of NVIDIA infrastructure, including Vera Rubin and Vera CPUs for next-generation AI agents to deliver maximum performance per watt. Meta will also deploy NVIDIA Spectrum-X™ Ethernet networking and BlueField-4® to support network efficiency and throughput. In addition, NVIDIA will invest $3 billion in Meta’s equity offering. “AI agents represent a new computing paradigm — software that understands our goals, reasons, uses tools and gets work done on our behalf,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “This changes how we use computers, from operating applications to working with intelligent agents. NVIDIA and Meta are expanding our partnership to optimize the computing infrastructure end to end for capable, efficient and secure AI agents, so Muse can empower billions of people to achieve more and pursue greater ambitions.” “Muse is how we bring personal superintelligence to everyone. We’re excited to keep working with NVIDIA to deliver the best personal agents and frontier models for billions of people,” said Mark Zuckerberg, founder and CEO of Meta.

cards.body: AI 추천 뉴스 네이버 '글로벌 AI팩토리' 닻 올렸다 브룩필드와 90억弗 인프라 계약 엔비디아, 네이버 3대주주로 '3자 연합모델'로 경쟁력 확보 네이버와 엔비디아, 브룩필드가 함께 추진하는 ‘글로벌 인공지능(AI) 팩토리’ 구축 사업이 본격화한다. 네이버가 브룩필드로부터 90억달러(약 12조원) 규모의 컴퓨팅 인프라를 확보하는 계약을 27일 체결하면서 엔비디아는 네이버에 10억달러(약 1조3300억원) 규모의 지분 투자를 이행해야 한다. 네이버는 이날 “브룩필드로부터 90억달러 규모의 컴퓨팅 인프라를 확보하는 계약을 맺었다”며 “엔비디아의 전략적 지분 투자를 위한 선결 조건을 충족했다”고 공시했다. 계약에 따라 브룩필드는 특수목적법인(SPV)인 ‘애셋코(Asset Co.)’를 설립하고 그래픽처리장치(GPU)와 데이터센터 등 컴퓨팅 인프라 자산을 네이버에 제공한다. 구체적인 GPU와 데이터센터 규모는 공개하지 않았다. 네이버는 이렇게 확보한 GPU와 데이터센터 등으로 가칭 ‘네이버 AI팩토리’를 운영하면서 국내 대기업 고객사에 AI 컴퓨팅 서비스를 판매하는 역할을 맡는다. 매출이 발생할 때마다 애셋코에 사용료를 지급한다. 네이버 AI팩토리 운영은 네이버클라우드가 주도하기로 했다. 네이버는 대기업 고객사 여러 곳과 계약 협상을 진행 중인 것으로 전해졌다. 이번 계약으로 네이버는 엔비디아를 대상으로 한 10억달러 규모 제3자 배정 유상증자 절차에도 속도를 낼 방침이다. 증자가 완료되면 엔비디아는 네이버 주식 4.5%(신주 724만1564주)를 취득해 국민연금, 블랙록에 이어 3대주주에 오른다. 네이버와 엔비디아, 브룩필드 3자 연합의 ‘AI 팩토리’ 사업의 핵심은 자본·기술·운영 역량을 나눠 맡는 구조에 있다. 엔비디아는 자본과 차세대 고성능 컴퓨팅 플랫폼 관련 기술을 제공하고, 브룩필드는 GPU와 데이터센터 등 인프라 자산을 확보한다. 네이버는 대규모 데이터센터를 직접 건립하거나 GPU를 매입하는 데 필요한 초기 자금 부담을 줄이면서 AI 인프라 사업을 신성장 동력으로 확보할 수 있게 됐다. 엔비디아는 자사 기술 기반의 컴퓨팅 인프라 생태계를 확장하고, 브룩필드는 인프라 투자 자산에서 수익을 창출하는 구조다. 글로벌 클라우드·AI 인프라 기업이 대규모 투자에 따른 자금 조달 부담을 안고 있는 상황에서 이번 사업 모델에 관심이 쏠렸다. 글로벌 네오클라우드 기업 코어위브의 회사채 금리는 한때 연 15%까지 치솟으며 자금 조달 비용에 대한 우려가 부각됐다. 업계에서는 AI 인프라 경쟁의 무게중심이 단순한 설비 확충에서 투자 효율과 재무 안정성으로 옮겨갈 수 있다는 전망이 나온다. 정지은 기자 jeong@hankyung.com

cards.body: 메타가 인공지능(AI)과 연산 인프라 구축을 위해 전날 발표했던 자금조달 규모를 25억 달러 늘리기로 했다. 메타의 증자 공모에는 발행 물량의 5배에 달하는 매수 주문이 몰리는 등 시장 관심이 집중됐다. 메타는 기존에 발표한 A형(클래스 A) 보통주 공모 규모를 애초 계획했던 225억 달러에서 250억 달러로 상향 조정했다고 27일(현지시간) 밝혔다. 이에 따라 메타의 이번 자금조달 전체 규모는 950억 달러에서 975억 달러(약 129조원)로 확대됐다. 메타는 A형 보통주 공모가를 발표 전 마지막 거래일인 지난 23일 종가(642달러) 대비 약 2.7% 할인한 625달러(약 83만원)로 확정했다. 이에 따라 공모 물량은 4000만주가 됐다. 함께 진행되는 전환우선주 공모는 주당 50달러에 2억5000만주 발행하는 것으로 결정됐다. 이번 보통주 공모 증자에는 발행 물량의 약 5배에 달하는 청약 주문이 들어오는 등 시장에서 크게 흥행했다고 블룸버그 통신이 소식통을 인용해 보도했다. 물량의 절반 이상은 장기 투자자와 기존 주주에게 배정됐으며, 상위 15개 기관투자자가 전체 물량의 70%를 인수했다. 전환우선주 공모도 몇 배에 달하는 초과 청약을 기록했다. AI 반도체 핵심 파트너사들의 지분 투자도 확정됐다. 엔비디아는 메타의 이번 주식 공모에 30억 달러(약 4조원)를, AMD는 10억 달러(약 1조3000억원)를 투자한다고 각각 밝혔다. 젠슨 황 엔비디아 최고경영자(CEO)는 “연산 인프라를 처음부터 끝까지 최적화하기 위해 메타와의 파트너십을 확장하고 있다”고 설명했다. 앞서 메타는 AI 인프라 확충과 개인용 초지능(SI) 개발 자금 확보를 위해 보통주·전환우선주 증자와 최근 신설한 C형(클래스 C) 무의결권 주식 장내 매각을 합해 총 950억 달러의 자금 조달에 나선다고 전날 발표했다. 메타는 3분기 잉여현금흐름(FCF)이 21억2000만 달러 적자로 돌아서는 등 자금 압박이 거세지자 이에 대응해 자금 조달에 나선 것으로 풀이된다. 정현정 기자 iam@etnews.com - 정현정 기자기사 더보기 - ET Events

headlines.body: Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices have said they will invest a total of $4 billion in Meta after the social media and artificial intelligence giant announced plans to raise $95 billion to support its investments in AI infrastructure. Meta on Monday said it would initially raise $35 billion in underwritten public equity offerings, before raising an additional $60 billion with an at-the-market program. Nvidia on Tuesday said it would invest $3 billion in Meta's equity offering, with AMD announcing it would invest $1 billion. Meta's Monday announcement said Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom were interested in purchasing up to $5 billion in shares. Nvidia, AMD deepen Meta ties Nvidia announced its investment on Tuesday, adding that Meta would expand Vera Rubin and Vera CPU deployment, and that the two companies would deepen their partnership on Muse, the social media giant's AI agent that launched last month. "AI agents represent a new computing paradigm — software that understands our goals, reasons, uses tools and gets work done on our behalf," said Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in a statement. "This changes how we use computers, from operating applications to working with intelligent agents." "We're excited to keep working with NVIDIA to deliver the best personal agents and frontier models for billions of people," said Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg. AMD said that its Helios racks were running at Meta and its EPYC processors were powering Meta's Muse. "Together, we are building and deploying infrastructure at gigawatt scale and shaping future generations of silicon, software and systems to enable Meta's most ambitious superintelligence models and services," AMD CEO Lisa Su said in a statement. AMD was up 3% on Tuesday, while Nvidia stayed flat. Meta was down 1%. Nvidia and AMD have been rapidly building up stakes in companies powering the AI boom. Nvidia has invested in OpenAI, Anthropic, Intel and XAI and participated in 121 investment rounds so far this year, according to Dealroom, up from just 13 in 2022. AMD in July said it would make an equity investment of up to $5 billion in Anthropic. The company has been involved in 25 funding rounds in 2026, up from just two in 2022.

headlines.body: TSMC is weighing raising prices for its Chip on Wafer on Substrate (CoWoS) advanced packaging technology by as much as 20%, reports Trendforce , citing supply chain sources and local media. The increase reflects strained capacity amid AI demand and longer delivery times for chipmaking tools. Such a hike would be significant, as CoWoS is already one of the tightest links in the AI supply chain. TSMC has yet to confirm the report. Go deeper with TH Premium: Chipmaking (Image credit: tsmc) Analyzing TSMC's fab expansion roadmap — multi-fab N2 ramp, CoWoS, SoIC, and uncorking bottlenecks Leading-edge foundry roadmaps for TSMC, Intel, and Samsung ASML's roadmap for chipmaking lithography tools examined Chinese chipmaking tool roadmaps examined CoWoS combines logic dies and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) stacks within a single package, which is how AI accelerators get the data bandwidth that demanding workloads require. Building these packages is only getting harder as chip designers cram in more compute and memory. Nvidia’s Blackwell already pairs two large GPU dies with eight HBM3E stacks, whereas the upcoming Rubin and Rubin Ultra are expected to push integration further, which will increase pressure on packaging and the supply chain that supports it. Testing is turning into another bottleneck. Blackwell reportedly takes three to four times longer to test than Nvidia’s previous-generation Hopper, and Rubin could need as much as seven times longer. Extended test cycles keep equipment occupied for longer, which makes it harder to increase output as demand grows. GPUs are not the only products competing for capacity either, as server CPUs and custom ASICs also need advanced packaging, adding more strain to an already crowded supply chain. Tools are also taking longer to arrive, as equipment lead times have reportedly stretched from three to six months to as long as eight months, making timely access to fab equipment increasingly important. As a result, TSMC has reportedly placed this year’s equipment orders at existing prices instead of negotiating discounts or extra features — a departure from its customary approach of using its purchasing power to secure better terms. Essentially, getting the tools on time now appears to matter more to the company than getting them cheaply. The squeeze echoes a report from September, which said that TSMC’s projected semiconductor equipment requirements had almost doubled in six months as the company expanded production to meet AI demand. Cliff Hou, deputy co-COO at TSMC, said that by July the company’s expected equipment needs had reached 1.9 times its original estimate as AI demand accelerated. “Compared with the pattern 30 years ago, we have never seen the demand increase that much, that frequency of changes,” Hou said at the time. headlines.body: On October 21, during GTC Berlin, Nvidia announced several massive, multi-billion-dollar deals with supply chain partners across substrates, advanced packaging, semiconductor testing, and optical engines to expand production capacity. Aimed at overcoming severe bottlenecks restricting the current and future AI infrastructure buildouts, the deals feature commitments and production roadmaps stretching through 2028, securing capacity for Nvidia and ensuring resiliency and redundancy in its AI accelerator supply chain. “We are in the midst of the largest infrastructure buildout in human history. Demand is extraordinary. Capacity is the constraint,” said Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. “Our supply chain partners are the world’s best manufacturers. I’m grateful they are expanding capacity around the globe to scale production and help us deliver the AI supercomputing systems powering this new industrial revolution.” The deals cover two major AI accelerator supply chain categories: hardware interconnects and OSAT (Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test). Under hardware interconnects, Nvidia is securing capacity for both substrates and co-packaged optics. Nvidia has signed deals with Ibiden, Unimicron, and Samsung Electro-Mechanics — three of the world's five largest substrate manufacturers — to support its production capacity expansion and reserve significant portions of that capacity for the chipmaker. The company says it plans to secure 2.5x dedicated substrate capacity over the next three years. Nvidia has also signed agreements with SPIL (Siliconware Precision Industries Co., Ltd) to expand manufacturing capacity for the optical engines used in co-packaged optics by 15x by mid-2027. On the OSAT side, Nvidia and Amkor are targeting a 300% increase in interposer wafer capacity by the end of 2028 through expanded advanced packaging capacity in South Korea, to support higher production volumes for Nvidia's platform. The company also plans to double its semiconductor testing capacity by 2027, investing $1.1 billion to reserve capacity from KYEC (King Yuan Electronics Co., Ltd.), the world's largest semiconductor testing company, which currently handles nearly all of Nvidia's chip testing. Nvidia currently leads the AI chip market by a considerable margin, with its extremely powerful accelerators sitting in a vast majority of AI data centers globally. These deals target major bottlenecks in the AI chip supply chain, suggesting Nvidia doesn't plan to relinquish its position soon. So, why these specific deals? What are the exact details? README:  # **Interactive World Simulation with Cosmos for Physical AI** **[Cosmos3 Examples Collection](https://huggingface.co/collections/nvidia/cosmos3-examples)** | **[Code](https://github.com/nvidia/cosmos)** | **[Technical Report](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/cosmos-lab/cosmos-simulation/technical-report.pdf)** (coming soon) | **[Website](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/cosmos-lab/cosmos-simulation/)** # Model Overview: Cosmos3-Nano-Transfer-Auto The highlighted checkpoint, Cosmos3-Nano-Transfer-Auto, is a post-trained variant of the Cosmos3-Nano base model. ## Description Cosmos3-Nano-Transfer-Auto generates synchronized multi-view camera videos and LiDAR observations. It supports up to 11 standard and fisheye camera views. Generation is conditioned on a text prompt, World Scenario Map (WSM) controls for each camera view, and aligned LiDAR controls when LiDAR output is requested. The WSM inputs encode driving-scene structure, including traffic signs, traffic lights, lane markings, and object cuboids, while the text prompt specifies appearance attributes such as weather, lighting, and time of day. This enables the same driving scenario to be regenerated at scale with controlled variations in scene appearance. The model uses bidirectional generation for batch synthetic data generation and serves as the source checkpoint for causal distillation into Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Auto, which provides closed-loop simulation with the same multi-view, multi-sensor output modalities. headlines.body: As the AI boom strains computing capacity, Nvidia has backed Indian startup Simplismart in a $14 million funding round, betting on software that helps companies run AI models more efficiently and, in some cases, with fewer GPUs. Nvidia participated in the all-primary Series B round alongside Accel, Shastra VC, and Micromax, with Dallas Venture Capital leading the investment. The deal values the four-year-old startup at about $100 million, including the new funding. Companies are nowadays spending heavily on GPUs to power AI applications, but running those models reliably and economically at scale remains a challenge. Different workloads demand distinct trade-offs between speed, cost, and performance. Deploying and operating AI models to meet business requirements often also requires complex adjustments. Simplismart says its software automates much of that work, tailoring how models run on existing computing infrastructure instead of requiring customers to manage those configurations themselves. “Nobody actually needs the fastest or the cheapest inference,” Amritanshu Jain (pictured above, left), co-founder and CEO of Simplismart, said in an interview. He added that companies instead need to run AI models at speeds and costs that make sense for their specific applications. Simplismart’s software sits between AI models and the computing infrastructure they run on and adjusts how models are deployed and managed to meet customers’ requirements. It says it can optimize factors such as how quickly a model responds, how many requests it handles, and how much computing power it consumes, helping companies get more out of their existing GPU stack. The Bengaluru-based startup offers companies a way to deploy and run AI models through its own platform or within their existing cloud and on-premises infrastructure. It also provides tools to fine-tune models, automatically scale computing resources as demand changes, and monitor performance. Additionally, Simplismart allows cloud providers to build and operate their own AI inference services on GPU infrastructure using its software. Simplismart says it helped AI video-generation platform InVideo cut its GPU serving costs by 56% using its software. The startup also works with AI video companies HeyGen and Higgsfield, as well as enterprise AI startup Ema, among others. Moreover, Indian cloud provider Yotta uses Simplismart’s technology to power the serverless AI inference service within its Shakti Studio platform. Simplismart’s annualized revenue run rate has grown 14-fold over the past six months to an eight-figure sum, Jain told TechCrunch. The figure is based on recent customer usage rather than contracted recurring revenue and excludes revenue passed through to infrastructure providers, the company said. He did not disclose the exact figure. More than half of Simplismart’s revenue comes from the U.S., despite the startup having more customers in India, Jain said. headlines.body: SoleCrypt has grown the size of a planned data center in Tunisia and provided details on the project timelines. The company last week announced plans for the SoleCrypt AI Campus in Bizerte. The first 7MW of the planned 40MW campus will be designed to host Nvidia’s HGX Rubin NVL8 hardware. The first phase, designed to deploy 1,728 Nvidia Rubin GPUs, could go live in early 2028. Full details haven’t been shared, but the project will reportedly be located approximately 3.6 km (2.23 miles) from the Medusa subsea cable landing site in Bizerte, via a routed fiber path. SoleCrypt said the development is supported by a dedicated 60MW solar and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project across 100 hectares, some 525km (326 miles) away in Tozeur. Launched in 2022, SoleCrypt focuses on developing data centers powered by solar assets. The company previously outlined plans to develop a 20MW data center in Bizerte. SoleCrypt signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Safozi, a Tunisian cloud and data infrastructure provider, late last year. The first phase of the Medusa cable, linking Marseille in France and Bizerte in Tunisia, went live earlier this year.
